chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad ibn al-Warraq, who said:

I presented to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a book in which was the Quran, sealed and adorned with gold, and a chapter was written at its end with gold. So he showed it to him, but he did not fault anything in it except the writing of the Quran with gold, and said: 'I do not like it if the Quran is written except with black (ink), just as it was written the first time.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq dislike the Quran being written in gold?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s preference for the traditional black ink (*as-sawad*) over gold, emphasizing humility and the preservation of the Quran’s original aesthetic as established during the Umayyad and early Abbasid periods. While the gold adornment (*mu'ashhar*) was not rejected, the specific restriction on the text itself reflects a scholarly consensus on maintaining the distinct visual identity of the Quranic script against mere decorative excess. This preference underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophet’s and Imams’ established practices (*sunan*) in the presentation of the Divine Word.
